subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation — Finovate
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Brown <sarah.brown@finovate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation — Finovate

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Recent availability incidents: three production outages in the past 6 months (partial service downtime on 2026-07-21 lasted ~2 hours).
- Failover is manual today: your team runs a scripted failover to a secondary provider; no automatic model/region fallback.
- Latency spikes during peak trading windows causing timeouts in downstream microservices.
- Cost pressure on serving—especially tail latency in larger models driving up token spend.

Current stack:
- Primary: Proprietary LLM endpoints hosted on a managed endpoint provider (us-east).
- Secondary: Smaller, in-house distilled model used for batch workloads.
- Orchestration: homegrown proxy layer; limited KV cache across requests.

Success criteria you called out:
- 99.95% availability for inference endpoints during market hours (SLA target).
- p95 end-to-end latency < 120ms for the signature risk-check route.
- Automatic graceful degradation to a smaller model or cached responses under load/failure, preserving core functionality.
- Auditability/audit logs for requests (retention 12 months).

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Multi-region routing + automatic failover: route by latency and capacity; automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in a different region.
2) Graceful degradation policy: when latency or error rate crosses threshold, route to a quantized/smaller model or return a reduced structured response instead of a full generation.
3) Prefix/KV caching for common request patterns to reduce cost and tail latency.
4) SLO monitoring + alerting hooks + runbooks integrated into your on-call workflow.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll share a short architecture note showing how Redwood would implement multi-region failover and graceful degradation for the risk-check flow — attached.
- Follow-up technical deep-dive with your infra lead (Tom) and our runtime team: propose Tue/Wed next week.
- Provide a draft mutual action plan and a scoping checklist so we can size dedicated capacity vs hosted.

Attachments: redwood-runtime-arch.pdf (architectural sketch), finovate-incident-log-2026Q2.xlsx (incident summary you shared).

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and share the MAP + estimated SLO/latency profile for the signature route.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
redwood.com
From: Sarah Brown <sarah.brown@finovate.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation — Finovate

Thanks Ben — this is an excellent recap and captures the call. A couple clarifications:

- The 2026-07-21 outage was caused by a noisy neighbor on the provider side, which caused degraded GPU availability in us-east. Failover to our secondary region (us-west) exists but requires manual steps and a data-sync that takes ~30–45 minutes.
- Our current contractual SLA with the provider is 99.9% but we’d need 99.95% for customer-facing risk checks.
- For graceful degradation we want to ensure the response still includes a structured decision (e.g., PASS/FLAG) even if the full explanation is shortened.

Tom (cc’d) will own the technical deep-dive scheduling. He’s available Tue 8/18 and Wed 8/19 mornings PST.

We also want a rough estimate of expected cost delta if we added multi-region active-active with automatic failover vs our current single-region setup.

Best,
Sarah

Sarah Brown
Head of Engineering, Finovate Systems
sarah.brown@finovate.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation — Finovate

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Sarah’s confirmation and their asks. TL;DR: Finovate wants SLA to 99.95% for risk-checks, automatic region/model fallback, and structured-response fallback during degradation. They asked for:

1) Architecture note (attached) for multi-region automatic failover and graceful degradation patterns.
2) Rough cost delta estimate for active-active multi-region vs single-region.
3) A proposed mutual action plan and a scoping checklist.

Can we: 1) put together a 1-pager showing the runtime changes (KV cache, model-variant routing, auto-fallback) and expected p95/p99 latency targets; 2) get a ballpark cost delta for a modest active-active deployment (estimate monthly committed cost + projected token/unit cost impact)?

Jonas — can you and runtime lead take the architecture note and identify any blockers for automatic model variant fallback (quantization/compatibility)?
Marissa — I’ll draft the MAP template and include the compliance/audit log retention items.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate scheduling with Tom for Tue/Wed next week.

Ben
